name: Wall-Facing Handstand Push-Up
description: The wall-facing handstand push-up positions the chest toward the wall rather than the back, forcing the body into a truly vertical and hollow position. This variation eliminates the arch that commonly occurs in the back-to-wall version and requires more core control. It is used as a bridge to the freestanding HSPU and trains the same deltoid and triceps musculature with more demanding postural requirements.

execution.starting_position: Walk feet up the wall while facing it until the chest is close to the wall. Hands on the floor, chest touching or very close to the wall, body vertical.
execution.setup_instructions: Begin from a push-up position facing the wall. Walk the feet up while walking the hands closer. Find the vertical with the chest against the wall.
steps: Step 1: Establish the chest-to-wall handstand position.
Step 2: Lower the head toward the floor slowly.
Step 3: Descend to full range — head touches the floor.
Step 4: Press back to full arm extension.
Step 5: Maintain chest contact or near-contact with the wall.
common_mistakes: Letting the hips pike away from the wall during the press
Losing the vertical body line and reverting to an arched position
safety_considerations: Have a mat under the head for protection
Prerequisites: comfortable back-to-wall HSPU for multiple reps
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full arm extension to head on the floor.
coaching_cues: Chest stays close to the wall
Press all the way to lockout
